clue.text: Tired and honest eccentric appears in article at a scandalously high price

indicators.note: the following pieces sit inside the word for article, so they are the contents of a container

parts.note: THE is the definite article
feeling rough means feeling worn out and unwell

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of honest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weary but honest oddball turns up in a newspaper piece about outrageous overcharging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired' looks like part of the definition but supplies a word for feeling unwell; 'eccentric' rearranges the honest letters, and 'appears in' splits the article around everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay through the nose is an idiom for paying far more than something is worth.

clue.text: Explosive launcher skirting rear of range is very dangerous

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
explosive suggests blowing apart, so the letters of launcher are scattered and rearranged
the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A rocket launcher placed around the back of a firing range is a real hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' turns LAUNCHER into HERCULAN, and 'skirting' wraps that around E, the last letter of 'range'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean tasks, like the labours of the hero Hercules, demand enormous strength and courage and carry great peril.

clue.text: Flower in neat border

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, a single one being an ox
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A bloom grows at the tidy edge of a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' here is the archaic word for cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild primula with pale yellow blooms, related to the cowslip.

clue.text: Entertainer in car gets to acknowledge abandoned site

indicators.note: the entertainer word sits within the letters for the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a type of sports car
a host entertains guests
to own is to admit or acknowledge

explanation.surface: A performer travelling in a car stops to recognise a deserted place.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted settlement whose inhabitants have all left is known by this phrase.

clue.text: Emperor becoming tense in raised plea

indicators.note: the letter for tense is placed within the turned-up plea word
in a down clue, raised means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a suit is a petition or legal plea
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An emperor grows nervous while making an elevated appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the plea word upside down in this down entry, and 'in' slips the tense letter into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman ruler of the Flavian dynasty, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: A mastery of construction?

parts.note: reads like skill in building, but means skill in constructing fine sentences and speeches

explanation.surface: Someone shows great skill at erecting buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The construction is of words and sentences, not bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, persuasive speaking is a skill in shaping language well.

clue.text: Cat in spring scratching head

indicators.note: scratching out the head means removing the first letter of the spring word

parts.note: bounce means spring or rebound

explanation.surface: A cat in a leap pauses to scratch its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called the ounce, a big wild feline of Central Asia.

clue.text: Third character in crew at the back from Asia

indicators.note: picks out the letter in third position of the word that follows

parts.note: astern means at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: The third member of a ship's crew sits at the stern, having come from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental lands, such as China and Japan, lie in this direction from Europe.

clue.text: Old Roman taking fixed course in vehicle

indicators.note: the fixed-course word goes within the vehicle word

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a rut is a groove or set routine

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman travels a set route aboard a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was the Roman senator who helped assassinate Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Country backing popular urge in part

indicators.note: backing means the letters found are read from right to left
only part of the phrase popular urge is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A nation supports a popular desire, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' takes LARUR from 'popuLAR URge', and 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, country means of the countryside, as in country life.

clue.text: Expenditure created by gregarious son

parts.note: a gregarious person is sociable and extrovert

explanation.surface: Spending is run up by a sociable young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out, or costs, are a business's or household's expenses.

clue.text: Politician inspired by right time to celebrate

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the politician goes inside the word for right

parts.note: true means correct or right
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician is encouraged by the perfect moment to rejoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' means taken into, not motivated by.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet an achievement is to proclaim and laud it loudly.

clue.text: Girlfriend in fleece

definitions.meaning: to fleece is to extort money from someone, to bleed them dry

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a sweetheart, and a verb for extorting money by pressure.

clue.text: Woman left fellow in terrace

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman abandoned a man in a row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrace' is a flat ledge of land, not a street of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge or flat raised step of rock or land, as on a continental margin.

clue.text: Move forcibly end of barrier amid confusion over protest

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
the letter goes in the middle of the confusion word

parts.note: a fog is a state of bewilderment

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: Push through the far side of a barricade amid chaos ahead of a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' puts R, the end of 'barrier', inside FOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone along by holding their arms from behind, as police may.

clue.text: Noon trip planned to go round good place in Kent

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the next piece
planned means arranged anew, so the letters of noon trip are reordered

explanation.surface: A midday excursion is arranged to tour a good spot in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges NOON TRIP; 'to go round' puts G inside. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpington is a town in the historic county of Kent, now in Greater London.

clue.text: A combination that puts one in good odour?

definitions.text: A combination that puts one in good odour?

parts.words: A combination that puts one in good odour?
parts.note: to be in good odour is an idiom for being in favour; here a mix that literally smells nice

explanation.surface: Some alliance wins one favour with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good odour' means well regarded, but the clue takes it literally: a scented mix of petals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of dried petals and spices is a fragrant mixture.

clue.text: Routine activity rated badly by philosopher

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of rated are put in poor order

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker gives a poor score to some everyday chore.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, repetitive grind of work is likened to an endless mill wheel.

clue.text: Summer protection best on nun possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters might be in another order

explanation.surface: A nun might be the finest choice for sheltering in the hot months.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed hat shades the head and neck from hot sun.

clue.text: Fruit is a necessity when from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read upward from the bottom

parts.note: a must is something essential
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Fruit becomes essential when coming from southern parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' reads A MUST AS upwards, giving the letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Figure putting head back? That's very likely!

indicators.note: the first letter of the number word is moved to the end

parts.note: seven is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A man tips his head back, sure something is about to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting head back' moves S from the front of SEVEN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds of one to one mean a strong chance, as good as anything.

clue.text: Dignified sound of spoken number

indicators.note: the sound of signals that the words are heard, not written

parts.note: said eight: spoken gives said, number gives eight

explanation.surface: A stately sound comes from a number someone calls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken number' is SAID EIGHT, which when heard matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm, composed and unhurried describes someone grave and stately.

clue.text: Flask drunk knocked back around island

indicators.note: the turned word wraps round the island
knocked back means the letters of the drunkard word are reversed

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Herm is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A bottle was downed, swigged near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is a noun, a drunkard, not the past participle; 'knocked back' turns it and 'around' wraps it round the small Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot or cold; the brand name became generic.

clue.text: More senior workman lacking introduction

indicators.note: the opening letter of the workman word is removed

parts.note: a welder is a metal worker

explanation.surface: An older tradesman goes without being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Older, higher in rank by age, as in an older sibling.

clue.text: Old-fashioned power

definitions.meaning: ... as in ... radio, informal for outdated technology
... is energy from heated water, as in ... engines

explanation.definitionFit: Vapour drives engines; and in steam radio it means quaintly dated.

clue.text: Exaggerated beginning to opera by composer and director

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Verdi was an Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: An opening to an opera by an Italian and a director went over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Took to excess, laid it on too thick.

clue.text: Values in market hiccuping

definitions.note: the plural definition matches a singular noun naming a set of moral principles

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words market hiccuping

explanation.surface: Prices in a stock market having the jitters.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral code or set of principles, as in the work ethic.

clue.text: University wanderer stumbling, slips maybe

indicators.note: stumbling means tripping up, so the letters of wanderer are muddled

explanation.surface: A college rambler trips and slips over.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are petticoats, an example of garments worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Lift given by army around Italy

indicators.note: the army word goes round the letter for Italy

parts.note: a host is a large army
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A ride is offered by soldiers in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or haul up, often by rope or crane.

clue.text: President and chairman? Nob all misjudged

indicators.note: misjudged suggests getting things wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A head of state and a company boss are snobs, all wrongly assessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln was the sixteenth leader of the United States.
